entries.title: The bathtub
entries.question: If the tap runs faster than the drain, what happens to the water in the tub?
lessons: A stock changes only through its flows
Net flow, not the flows alone, sets the direction
entries.source: Written for Dynamist from a textbook structure; no third-party file or text.

entries.title: Births and deaths
entries.question: Why does a population grow when births exceed deaths, and what does each loop do on its own?
lessons: Each loop is read on its own, then together
Loop polarity decides growth or decay

entries.title: A shipment delay
entries.question: Orders step up. When do the goods arrive, and how does the kind of delay change the answer?
lessons: The kind of delay changes the shape of the response, not only its timing

entries.title: Hiring and stock: oscillation
entries.question: Demand steps up. Why do the workforce and inventory swing before they settle?
lessons: A balancing loop with a delay overshoots
Damping depends on adjustment times
entries.source: Structure after Hayward and Roach (2023, Fig. 5): three balancing loops. The diagram is theirs; the formulas, names and numbers are the standard ones for this structure, written by us. No text, table or file of the paper is included.
entries.licence: Same licence as the Dynamist project (own work); free to use, copy and teach with.

entries.title: Growth runs into a limit
entries.question: Why does growth that starts exponential slow down and level off?
lessons: Dominance shifts from the reinforcing to the balancing loop
The limit shapes the curve long before it is reached

entries.title: A fishery: testing a policy
entries.question: How hard should boats fish to bring home the most fish over fifty years?
lessons: Pushing a lever harder is not always better
A policy is judged on a horizon and a measure

entries.title: Which lever matters?
entries.question: Six numbers could be changed. Which ones decide the outcome, and which can be left alone?
lessons: Most inputs do not matter; find the few that do before studying them
Loop dominance explains why
